messages:
alex_warden: Heads-up — we're seeing a wave of GPU nodes go NotReady in us-west1-a. Started ~14:10 UTC, ~8 nodes. kubelet logs show device-plugin errors. Anyone on this?

maria_ops: Which nodepool? gpu-pool-usw1? Any recent node image/kernel bump?

sre_oncall: Confirmed, nodes from nodepool "gpu-pool-usw1" — cluster-autoscaler also triggered a scale-up but new nodes fail to register Ready.

alex_warden: Yep gpu-pool-usw1. No infra deploys in last 2 hours. I grabbed a kubelet/device-plugin log from one instance:

julian_l: ```
Sep 21 14:09:52 ip-10-0-3-45 kubelet[1023]: E0921 14:09:52.331 device-plugin.go:214] Handler for preStartContainer failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start device plugin: timeout waiting for driver init
Sep 21 14:09:54 ip-10-0-3-45 kernel: nvidia: probe of nvidia0 failed with error -110
Sep 21 14:09:55 ip-10-0-3-45 systemd[1]: nvidia-module-load.service: Start request repeated too quickly
```

maria_ops: That -110 probe/timeout smells like the nvidia kernel module failing to load — possibly a mismatched module vs kernel ABI. Any recent kernel updates on that node image?

sre_oncall: Looking at image builder pipeline: we shipped a minor kernel patch in the node image last week for CVE backports. It's possible the pinned nvidia-driver version is incompatible.

alex_warden: Quick workaround: I'm tainting the pool (kubectl taint nodes -l pool=gpu-pool-usw1 dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule) to stop scheduling critical jobs and prevent noisy autoscaler churn.

julian_l: Also checked device-plugin pods in kube-system: many in CrashLoopBackOff. `kubectl -n kube-system get pods | grep nvidia` shows plugin restarting with: `failed to initialize: driver not ready`.

buildbot: cluster-autoscaler: scaleUp triggered for gpu-pool-usw1 (3 -> 6) at 14:12:05 UTC

maria_ops: Ops question: are these preemptible/spot nodes? If they're spot, the autoscaler could be mixing instance types with different kernel/ami refreshes making it intermittent.

sre_oncall: These are mixed: 70% preemptible, 30% on-demand. But boot logs show identical AMI. Still, kernel module load can fail if initramfs doesn't include required symbols.

alex_warden: Plan: 1) cordon/taint pool (done), 2) pin workloads to fallback CPU-only pool, 3) roll node image back to previous AMI for gpu-pool and re-create nodes, 4) open infra-ops ticket to rebuild driver package with DKMS. Any objections?

julian_l: +1. For faster mitigation we can push a device-plugin restart with extra wait-for-driver probe logic (see runbook snippet). Will open a small hotfix PR to add a 60s probe retry before CrashLoopBackOff.

maria_ops: Note on cost: autoscaler kept flapping and created 3 extra nodes that never served work — taking spot budget. Billing already flagged a small spike. We should add a cooldown to the gpu-pool autoscaler hook until image is validated.

alex_warden: Filed INF-3421: rollback gpu-pool AMI -> previous stable image. Also INF-3422 to add DKMS-driver build. I've kicked off a rollback instance group replace; nodes will drain and re-create over next 20m.

buildbot: infra: rolling-replace started for nodepool gpu-pool-usw1 (request id r-77d8) at 14:18:03 UTC

julian_l: After the first replacement node came up with old AMI, driver probe succeeded and node reached Ready at 14:25. I verified `nvidia-smi` returns GPUs and device-plugin pod transitioned to Running.

maria_ops: Great — please keep the pool tainted until 80% of nodes are validated. Also add a postmortem note about the image-driver coupling.

sre_oncall: Temporary mitigation checklist posted to runbook: "gpu-node-image-driver-mismatch". Will follow-up with DKMS rollout so kernel updates won't require manual driver rebuilds.

alex_warden: Thanks team. Closing immediate incident — will monitor autoscaler and billing impact tomorrow. :thumbsup:
